The rent was good, but I was in an odd living arrangement wherein a house had been broken into a four-unit apartment building. The landlord lived on the top floor, me and an elderly couple lived on the middle floor, and some friends of the landlord lived on the ground floor.

Apparently the landlord suffered from bipolar disorder, and his ex wife took care of all the bills and any issues we had with our unit. He wasn't really the best point of contact for things, as he would do stupid stuff like rip the phone line out of the wall when it rang too much. He also made me a bit uncomfortable as he would do weird stuff like have huge parties and ask if he could show off my (recently remodeled) unit to all his drunk friends.

The elderly couple across the way were pretty nice, but I didn't know very much about the neighbors below me, just that they had a curtain over their door and often had guests at all hours... of course at 19 and coming from a good upbringing I had no idea what this meant.

One night the tenant doorbell rang and there was a scuffle outside. I (foolishly) went down and opened the door to find a plainclothes cop at the door. He asked for the landlord and I sent him around front to the other door. There was a scuffle, some yelling, and then awkward silence. A few minutes later I heard sirens, and cops came to my door and escorted me out of the building behind bulletproof shelds. Across the street, snipers were aiming at the house. The entire street was full of black unmarked vehicles.

At this point it's about 11pm and I find myself in the back of a police supervisor vehicle. I'm trying to put together the pieces as I'm being questioned. No, I don't know the drug dealers downstairs. Yeah the landlord is a whacko. He did what?

Apparently the cops had come to bust a drug ring, and the landlord told them to get off his property or he'd set off a bomb and blow the enire place into the ground.

It took the bomb squad until 4am to determine that he was just an idiot and didn't have anything. They slid tear gas under his door and dragged him out.

I felt bad for the elderly couple because they had no place to go and weren't as comfortable sitting in a cop car listening to radio communications as I was.

Needless to say, I broke my lease and found another place to live.
